findings.claim: The eligibility gate for asking the notes turn only checks `spec.forbidden` and `policy.protected`, never `spec.touches` — even though `touches` is the scope-restricting mechanism declared on essentially every non-bug spec (and ratified for bug specs), and is one of the three inputs the `scope` gate itself checks (see the `scope_gate(diff, spec.touches, forbidden=spec.forbidden, protected=policy.protected)` call earlier in this file). The motivating scenario in the spec's own Problem section — 'wiring falsified four comments in files it could not touch' — and even this change's own test fixture text ('touches did not cover that file, so I left it as-is') describe an agent running into the `touches` boundary, not a `forbidden` or `protected` one. Because the heuristic omits `touches`, the notes turn will be silently skipped for the common case of a spec with a declared `touches` set but no `forbidden` list and no repo-wide `protected` path — exactly the class of omission items 71/75/80 were filed over — while the test suite only ever exercises specs that also declare `forbidden`, masking the gap.

`render_pr_body` is called here with every other outcome field (`reviews`, `rebut_result`, `effective_risk`, `advisory_gates`, ...) but never `notes=outcome.notes`. Since `notes` defaults to `""` on `render_pr_body`, this call site silently renders every real PR body without the implementer's notes section, so acceptance criterion 1 ("An implementer's notes reach the pull request body") is never actually satisfied in production even though extraction, hashing, `notes.json` persistence, and the `_notes()` renderer are all correctly implemented and unit-tested in isolation.

`notes_worth_asking = bool(spec.forbidden) or bool(policy.protected)` has its `protected` half completely unexercised: every notes-turn test in this diff pairs `forbidden=[...]` with either the default empty `protected` or an explicit non-empty `protected` on top of an already-true `forbidden`, and the only test with `protected` empty also has `forbidden` empty. Replacing the line with `notes_worth_asking = bool(spec.forbidden)` keeps every test in test_session.py green (test_the_notes_artifact_is_hashed_when_it_is_produced, test_notes_are_empty_when_the_implementer_has_nothing_to_report and test_the_notes_turn_is_skipped_once_the_task_is_over_budget all set `forbidden`; test_no_notes_turn_is_asked_for_when_nothing_could_have_been_denied sets neither). This matters concretely because Saffron's own `.saffron/policy.yaml` (this very repo, which drives its own specs) declares a permanently non-empty `protected` list and most specs do not declare `forbidden` at all — so in the repo the feature was written for, the turn's eligibility currently rides entirely on the `protected` clause, and that clause can be silently dropped without a single test noticing.
